He should not remain a slave to his cravings and desires. This is the standard that is necessary for human advancement. Among the nations of the world that have progressed, they have been such that they exercised restraint over their own selves. In their use of pleasant things there is moderation, and they have remained elevated above their desires. In human history, whenever a nation has become a slave to pleasures and a devotee of luxuries, it has fallen spiritually and reached the level of the animal.

This was the reason why Allah placed the first human in this trial, because he was to be prepared for the office of vicegerency on earth, since in this world only those people would lead a successful life who possess a strong willpower: those who can exercise self-restraint in the face of satanic glitter, satanic whisperings, and the acquisition and abundance of desirable things. This was the experience of man, the first experience of the first human being. Now the announcement of the result is made.

Where this story is narrated in summary, its details appear elsewhere, because here the aim is to show only that aspect of the story which concerns the favours bestowed upon the prophets. Therefore this brevity and summarization is for the purpose of quickly conveying the aspect of favour.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 20, verse 117:

One of the favours and blessings of Allah was that Allah had told Adam in advance that Shaytan is an enemy to you. "

One of the favours and blessings of Allah was that Allah had told Adam in advance that Shaytan is your enemy, because he refused to prostrate himself before Adam. Yet the command to prostrate had been given to him by Allah Himself. Allah had also indicated beforehand the plan for the creation of Adam.

﴿Then let him not drive you both out of the Garden, so that you come to misery﴾ (20:117). "Lest he drive you both out of the Garden, and you fall into hardship." For by leaving the Garden, man was brought face to face with toil, struggle, wrong action, misguidance, anxieties, bewilderment, longing and waiting, grief and deprivation. What greater hardship could there be? All these things awaited man outside the Garden. As long as Adam was in the Garden, he was safe from these hardships and troubles.

You shall not hunger therein nor go naked, nor thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun.

As long as you are in Paradise, all these comforts will be yours. Hunger and the lack of clothing, thirst and exposure to the sun are opposites, both literally and in meaning; together they form the set of needs that puts every human being to toil on this earth.

But Adam had not yet suffered the stumbles of life in Paradise; he had no experience of its trials. The human being is weak in nature, and the desire for everlasting life is a great human weakness. Moreover, when everlasting life is combined with firmly established authority, what more could a person want? It is through this very door that Satan enters into him.

The apparent meaning is that the private parts of the human being are intended, which were hidden from them. The places of modesty in the bodies of both... Therefore, out of their natural sense of shame, they began to cover those places and started wrapping upon them leaves of Paradise. It is also possible that as a result of eating the fruit of that tree, a sexual sensation arose within them, because until a person develops a sexual sensation, he does not feel shame. A person pays attention to these things only when sexual desire arises.

It is possible that Allah prohibited Adam and Hawwa from eating the fruit of that particular tree so that as a result bodily desires would arise in the human being, and Allah deferred them according to His plan. The occurrence of forgetfulness from Adam also happened because his connection with Allah decreased, and because of the domination of bodily desires over him, the sexual system came into being. It is also possible that their urge for eternity manifested in the form of sexual desires because of that tree, in that although an individual does not attain eternity, yet the survival of the human race exists in it. All these explanations appear reasonable in light of the reality that by eating that fruit their private parts were exposed.

Here it is not stated that ﴿فبدت لهما سوآتهما﴾ "Their private parts became exposed," rather it is said:

﴿فبدت لهما سوآتهما﴾ (20:121) "Their private parts became exposed to them." The meaning is that they had no awareness of them. Upon eating the fruit, they became aware of this human impulse. Elsewhere the Qur'an has expressed this reality in another way:

﴿ليبدي لهما ما وري عنهما من سوآتهما﴾ "So that He might expose to them what was hidden from them of their private parts." And elsewhere:

The garment may also refer to chastity, purity, and the garment of connection with Allah. In any case, these are various exegetical suppositions; we do not emphasize any one of them nor prefer any one over another. The purpose is only to determine the correct form of this first human experience in human life.

After this lapse, Allah's mercy enveloped Adam (peace be upon him) and his wife, because this was the first experience of humanity.

And this took place after Adam sought forgiveness from Allah, expressed remorse, and presented his excuse; and these matters are not mentioned here so that only the mercy of Allah may be seen here.

After this, both parties, Adam and Iblis, were now commanded: "Go down (from here) to the earth; you are enemies of one another. There will be a long struggle between you." This was only the first round of your conflict.

Thus enmity arose between these two groups of God's creation. So now the children of Adam cannot put forward the excuse that they had no knowledge that Satan is their enemy, and that they were destroyed in unawareness. For this reason, mankind was fully warned in advance, and it was proclaimed throughout the whole universe that:

﴿بعضكم لبعض عدو﴾ (20:123) "You two groups are enemies of one another." This proclamation, which echoed through the entire universe and in which all the angels were made witnesses, is the demand of God's mercy that Messengers be sent from time to time to guide mankind and to remind them. Accordingly, the enemy was announced, and then it was said that Messengers would also come, and after that you would be free to choose which path you take.

This scene comes after that story, so it may be part of that story. In reality, this announcement also took place in the higher realm after the event of Adam and Iblis. Therefore, this is an established principle for this whole universe from ancient times. It can be neither withdrawn nor amended.

﴿فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى﴾ (20:123) "So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be miserable." Such a person will be protected from error and calamity. Error and calamity lie in wait outside the gate of Paradise with great eagerness for you, but whoever follows My guidance will remain safe from them. Calamity is in fact the fruit of error. Even if the person who has gone astray is immersed in worldly goods, these goods are themselves a great calamity for the one who is astray. Calamity in this world and calamity in the Hereafter: however abundant unlawful livelihood may be in this world, it produces bitterness and difficulties in a person's life. As soon as a person departs from God's guidance, he enters darkness, gropes about here and there, and anxiety and distress become part of his life. Sometimes he runs this way, sometimes that way; his life becomes clearly unbalanced. In short, calamity accompanies the one who has gone astray, even if he is in luxury. A great misery awaits him in the Hereafter, while the one who walks on God's guidance is completely saved from error and calamity in this world, and in the Hereafter he will be in the Firdaws Paradise. There is only the delay until the Promised Day arrives.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 20, verse 124:**

﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life﴾ (02 : 321). ﴿قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيراً﴾ (02 : 521) "My Lord, in the world I was a person with sight. Why have You raised me up blind here?" Then the answer will come.

When a person focuses his mind and heart on the history of past nations that have been destroyed, and sees their ruins in the valleys and hills, then although these people perished long ago, their great personalities, their rushing figures, their movements and stillness, their aspirations and desires, their anxieties and their plans fill the human mind. Translation:

These people, with their disbelief, their mockery, their rebelliousness and their turning away, say whatever they say; do not be distressed by it, and do not wear yourself out on their account. Now the proof is established against them: you should worship your Lord morning and evening. The remembrance of God in the tranquil time of the morning, and the remembrance of God in the tranquility of the time of sunset, at which time this whole universe closes its eyes, and the remembrance of God in the two tranquil sides of night and day, bring great peace to hearts and are a cause of God's good pleasure.

Glorifying and praising God brings nearness to God, and one attains closeness through what is near to God. A person feels himself in the company of an extremely reassuring, peaceful and joy-giving Being, and finds shelter in His embrace of mercy. The fruit of glorification and worship is indeed the pleasure of God, but before that, inner peace and tranquility grow within the believer, and the springs of contentment burst forth. This is its luminous reward for the act. O Muhammad (ﷺ), while worshipping, turn towards God, and ﴿And do not extend your eyes to what We have given to pairs of them to enjoy, the splendor of the worldly life﴾ (20:131), ﴿the flower of the life of this world﴾ (20:131). The equipment of the world, the adornments and decorations, wealth and possessions, status and rank. The flower of the life of this world: this life appears in the way that a soft and delicate flower appears on a plant, shining and attractive, but the flower is quick to fade and wilt by evening, however very attractive. We test them by giving them this quickly fading flower of life; we see how these people behave with this flower.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 20, verse 131:

"And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting." (Qur'an 20:131) The provision given by Allah is a blessing, not a trial. Lawful provision is good and remains lasting; it neither deceives nor creates temptation.

This is not a call to abandon the life of this world, but it does carry the message that you should give importance to real and enduring values, and that these enduring values lie in one's relationship with Allah and in seeking His pleasure. People should not bow down before the worldly goods and possessions. We should not lose the quality of taking pride in lofty values. The worldly goods that dazzle the eyes: may they not lower your lofty gaze. Instead, remain exalted in the face of them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 20, verse 132:

"Enjoin prayer upon your family (ahl) and be steadfast in it" (Qur'an 2:231 as cited). A Muslim's first duty is to make his home a Muslim home. He should urge his family to perform the obligation that connects them to Allah, so that unity is established in his household. How fortunate is the home in which there is complete unity.

﴿And be steadfast in it.﴾ Establish the prayer fully. Create its effects within yourselves, for indeed prayer restrains from immorality and evil (munkarat). These are the true effects of prayer. When a household becomes firm in prayer, these effects arise from it, in its consciousness and in its every mode of conduct. If the effects of prayer do not appear, then the prayer is not truly established; it is merely movements and words.

This prayer, this worship, this connection with Allah and these obligations are not beneficial to Allah. He is free of need from them; they bring Allah no benefit.

﴿We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you.﴾ These acts of worship exist so that the fear of God may arise in your hearts. You are being given [provision]. "These acts of worship exist so that the fear of God may arise in your hearts. You are being given."

﴿And the good end is for righteousness (taqwa).﴾ A person derives benefit from these acts of worship both in this world and in the Hereafter. When he worships, he himself is pleased; he becomes content, attains tranquility, and in the Hereafter the reward of these acts also returns to him.

Now, at the end, comes a comment on those wealthy and influential people who used to demand of the Prophet ﷺ that he present some extraordinary miracle. They are told: is this Qur'an not sufficient for you?

This is obstinacy and stubborn denial. The demand was made merely for the sake of asking, otherwise is the miracle of the Qur'an not a sufficient miracle? The Qur'an links the present message with the messages that came before it. It presents the same teachings that earlier messengers presented, rather, the matters that were stated in brief there are here given in detail. Allah, the Exalted, has sent the Final Prophet (ﷺ) as a means of completing the proof (itmam al-hujjah).

This passage is Urdu, but the instruction says translate the passage. Here is the translation.

These people were not humiliated and disgraced at the time these verses of the Qur'an were being recited to them. Rather, this is a depiction of their predetermined end, in which they will certainly remain. These verses came to them as the establishment of proof (itmam-i hujjah), so that on the Day of Resurrection they could not say such a thing, and so that they would have no excuse or pretext left, saying, "No message came to us."

When matters had reached the point that their final end is that they are going to be humiliated and disgraced, the Qur'an commands the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to leave them to their state, for their decision has already been made.

"Hafa al-qalam bi-ma huwa ka'in" (the pen has dried over what is to be): do not be distressed that they do not believe. Declare: "Wait, you too, and I too am waiting."

This is how the surah concludes, returning to the theme with which it began: "We did not send down the Qur'an to you, O Prophet, to cause you distress, but as a reminder for those who fear God." Thus the ending of the surah is also in harmony with its beginning: "This is only a reminder for one who would be benefited by a reminder." Now that this reminder has reached you, what remains except to await the outcome? And the outcome is in the hands of God.
